contract: docs/contracts/recal-product-v1.md v3: 一次 arm 的 capture_plan 批量入口

api.function: replay_capture_plan(outputs, fixture_id, model_path, source_pcm16, *, request_id, scene_id, op, hp_volume, gain_q12, direct_only, zero_coeff, speaker_confirmed, local_capture_confirmed, restore_stock, before_start, cancel_event)

design: One fresh overlay download, one complete source load (all segments + 2-frame zero tail), one coefficient load (zero coefficients, direct_only/zero_coeff), one arm.
The 16384-frame ring is drained DURING the run in 2048-frame chunks aligned to each planned window; no second download, no replay of the tail window.
Each chunk is recorded in read_proof {first_frame, end_frame, completed_before, completed_after} and the driver aborts the whole batch with ring_overrun when completed_after - first_frame > 16384.

Each planned window is written as its own NPZ (16384 frames, coefficients_q20 zero, full batch source_pcm16, metadata_json with fixture/gain/hp/model/driver/bit/hwh/helper hashes) plus its own .status.json.
Each segment is verified with replay_tools.verify_replay against the full batch source and its global first_frame; bit_exact is required.
Any failure returns ok=false with failed_index/failed_check and captures=[] (whole-batch failure, no retry, no partial success).
No RTL / bitstream / algorithm / run-parameter change; C's recal_link/hw_api calling layer untouched.

design_estimate_do_not_quote_as_measurem.risk: if the Python MMIO read loop is slower than ~1x audio rate the ring overruns; the driver then fails the batch with ring_overrun instead of faking a tail window

If ring_overrun appears, A reduces per-frame MMIO ops (drop the two command echo reads after establishing the read latency on hardware) or lowers BATCH_CHUNK_FRAMES; both are driver-internal and do not touch RTL.
